items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He come out of that school with Ernest Trepannier, Alec Bigard, Henry Morton.

ctx.x: He played, when he played, he was [? (inaudible)], like he was dancing with a woman. That come out of ragtime. They kept them snare drums going. Raddy Jean Vigne and his [? (inaudible)] moustache, he’s good looking, pretty brown . . . He’s a master bricklayer and plasterer. Building trades. He didn’t play music for a living. He played, but he had more, make more money than ten bands, because he did all that masonry work in the French Quarter. They call him Raddy Jean Vigne. Baby Dodds and all the great drummers…
